findings.title: A tile Mix's chain (and Mix my boxes again's) runs at Settings' depth when the runner builds it, not the depth its review showed and its funding paid for
findings.scenario: 5 ₳ v2 pool, width 3, Settings depth 1. The user reviews a tile Mix of 10 boxes: "1 wave deep, 10 mixes, about 9.5 ₳". Funding is 10 × 5.95 + 1.5 = 61 ₳, plus the 1.5 ₳ tail reserve and the 5 ₳ collateral. The user sends it. Before the runner builds the chain (the funding landing, or the next unlock if the wallet locked first), the user sets Settings' depth to 3. The runner then plans at depth 3: per box 5 + 13 × 0.95 = 17.35 ₳, so (62.5 − 1.5 − 1.5) / 17.35 = 3 boxes (capped at the funded 10). The chain goes 3 boxes × 13 mixes = 39 mixes, about 32.6 ₳ at v2's measured 0.837 ₳. That is about 23 ₳ more in fees than the review said, and 15 ₳ goes into boxes instead of 50 ₳; about 14 ₳ comes back at once. In the reverse case (reviewed at depth 3, 175 ₳ funded, Settings changed to 1), all 10 boxes go at depth 1: 10 mixes instead of 130, each box one of 3 leaves instead of one of 27, and about 100 ₳ of fee money comes back. Nothing is shown, since the Mix runs itself. Mix my boxes again (`mix.again`) goes the same way.
findings.since: 7db81171 (chunk 16's tile Mix, before the first tag; in every tag from web-wallet/1.6.0). 52044817 (L21) later fixed only swaps.
findings.evidence:
sessions.ts:2330-2340, the record mixOutSubmit writes: `mix: { boxes, again?, publicToo?, bootstrap?, noCollateral?, pool?, width? }, auto: { approved: { minAmountOut: "0", fund: {...} } }`. It holds no depth and no `auto.lovejoin`.
sessions.ts:4667, buildBack's `fixed`: `record?.mix?.seed || record?.mix?.bootstrap ? 0 : record?.auto?.lovejoin?.depth`, which is undefined for a tile Mix.
lovejoin.ts:3701 (chain): `const depth = fixed ?? set.depth;` with `set = await this.settings()`, i.e. the preferences now. lovejoin.ts:3379 (plan): `const depth = fixed ?? (await this.settings()).depth;`.
lovejoin.ts:3747: `paid.set(w, Math.min(plan.boxes, boxes ?? plan.boxes, priced.boxes));` counts the funded boxes at the new depth.
lovejoin.rs:1642-1646 (chain_at) builds `request.depth` waves for `request.boxes` boxes, as told.
The review side: Lovejoin.tsx:2811 prices the form through `lovejoin-funding` with no depth (Settings' then). Lovejoin.tsx:3820 shows `lovejoin.review.depthMixesCost`: "{{count}} waves deep, {{mixes}}, about {{ada}} ₳".
The rule exists for swaps alone: sessions.ts:442-455 (AutoRecord.lovejoin, "Settings changes swaps started later (independent review L21)"). Width is kept for a Mix and depth isn't: wayOf (sessions.ts ~6413) `if (s?.mix) return { width: s.mix.width ?? 3 }`. Chunk 34's review item 4 fixed the width half of this class by recording `mix.width`.
Figures use core's constants: MIX_FEE_ESTIMATE 950,000, DEPOSIT_RESERVE 1,500,000, COLLATERAL_TAIL_RESERVE 1,500,000, `mixes_per_box_at(3,3) = 13`.
Nothing was run.
findings.fix: Record the depth (and the delay) on `record.mix` in mixOutSubmit, as `width` is: `...(built.mix.depth !== undefined ? { depth: built.mix.depth } : {})`. Have buildBack prefer it: `record?.mix?.seed || record?.mix?.bootstrap ? 0 : (record?.mix?.depth ?? record?.auto?.lovejoin?.depth)`. Do the same for `chainDelay` (sessions.ts:4695). Older records with no depth keep today's behaviour. Same family: `collateralIntoPool()` is also read at build, so a Mix whose review said its collateral is mixed sends the 5 ₳ back unmixed if the switch was turned off in between. This is L21's rule (a run keeps what its review showed) applied to the tile's Mix and Mix again. Test: a Vitest that funds a Mix at depth 1, changes preferences to 3, runs buildBack, and asserts the chain's `depth` and `boxes` are the review's.

checked_ok: Every core builder this file calls balances, checked overflow included: deposit_across (change = total − boxed − kept − fee), mix_with (change = payer + taken − fee, collateral return 5 ₳ − (3/2·fee + 1)) and withdraw_with in all three paying modes.
A collateral tail's deposit spends every coin it's given (deposit_across inputs all), so direct_tail's `rest` (the mix's change plus the unspent rows) neither drops nor double-spends a UTxO.

with_return puts no UTxO in both the chain and the return. The tail path replaces the chain's change and the collateral with the tail mix's change. `unsent` is exactly what isn't on chain (chain change, token change).
`returned = total − back_fee` can't wrap: a sweep pays its fee from `taken`, and a merged return's `taken` holds the session's own collateral (≥ 5 ₳) short of hundreds of own UTxOs.
withdraw_paid_in's `paid = payer − change` is fee + topped, so it can't underflow.

Reward balances: taken only by a successful build (mix_with, withdraw_with). PrivateTooSmall retries take nothing. A tail built then dropped touches no sent transaction. One balance per pool per call, so a chain and its tail in one pool take it once.
Width: every entry point checks 3 or 4 (check_width / Wide::width). The collateral's mix is always 3 wide. The worker's 4→3 fallback (narrower) catches any non-network WebAssembly error.
Depth: every builder is bounded 0..=3 (fresh_for, check_deposit/check_mix). The worker's depth comes from preferences validated on read and write (isLovejoinDepth) or from a record.

Funding sums: token totals are u128; chain_from_account's `needed` is checked; Holdings::spare's plain sum is the CLAUDE.md-documented case (honest rows can't wrap), and deposit_across re-checks the inputs' total.

No reachable trap in this file: slices are bounded by `.min(len)`, `paths[...]` keys all come from check_paths over the same rows, `deposit.boxes[0]` is on a one-owner deposit, `rows[0]` is pushed first, and core's `expect`s are counted.
Stranger rows: deep datums are skipped before any decode (parse_mix_datum within_depth, eval::refusal, unreadable_datum in protocol_of, koios lenient_value/some_script for the JSON).
PoolBox::from_row matches the payment credential only, as Lovejoin v2's input_at_script does, so a box under a stake key is a valid mix input. Mix outputs are enterprise, as output_at_script demands.
Lovejoin v2's reference_holder is always-False, so a stranger's copy of a pool script at the holder (pool_of picks the first by ref) is permanent and harmless as a reference input.
Register::is_owned refuses identity points, and register_of_datum is strict, so no planted UTxO every key owns can derail withdraw_private_in.
finish_with_collateral_key verifies giveme.my against the body hash; add_witnesses keeps the session key's witness and refuses any body change.
The worker passes `boxes` on every chain, computed from the plan at the same reserve; chain_at caps it by token_boxes / ours.len(). `request.pool` rows are real(split), reserved boxes excluded.
A public-paid withdraw's record carries the register's lovelace and no private fee; the public side reads from chain, so no false figure there.
A public mix's summary names the boxes' token and the ADA change; the deposit's unused tokens stay at 0/0, where the balance shows them.
notes: Unrealistic stranger-forced downgrade, for the owner: every ADA-only, evaluable row at the session's key is a `coin` that the chain's deposit (chain_at, chain_across_pools) and direct_tail spend all at once, with no size cap, unlike plan_return. About 400 small ADA-only UTxOs (~0.97 ₳ each at 4,310 lovelace a byte, ~40 bytes an input against 16 KiB, so ~400 ₳ gifted to the victim) make the deposit too large. The chain errors, buildBack's catch sets `skipped`, and the return comes back directly, unmixed. A swap's auto-return sends that without review. The cost makes it a note, not a finding.

Defence in depth: plan_at and plan_across_pools call mixes_per_box_at / *_affordable_in with no depth bound, unlike funding_at (check_deposit) and the builders (fresh_for). `width.pow(depth)` overflows usize at depth ≥ 21 (width 3) or ≥ 16 (width 4) on wasm32, trapping if core-compiled. Unreachable: the worker's depth is 0..3. A `0..=3` check at their top, as funding_at has, closes it.

Rust never refuses a deposit or a tail into a retired pool: Version::retired() has no caller. The worker's takesNewBoxes / isRetired / adaPoolOf / tailChain are the only guards. Not reachable by a stranger or a site.

collateral_mix (lovejoin.rs:523) checks only the payer's key. The other `request.utxos` go into the sweep unchecked, where holdings_of and session_return check every row. The worker passes the session's own rows; a row under another key would only make the sweep unsignable (refused at submit). A nit.
lovejoin.rs's payment_key (:69) doesn't check the address's network, unlike api's payment_key_of. No reachable harm, since the ledger refuses wrong-network outputs.

Same family as w3#1: Settings' collateral switch (collateralIntoPool) is read at build too, so turning it off between a Mix's review (which said the collateral is mixed) and its build sends the 5 ₳ back unmixed and the 1.5 ₳ reserve back. The user's own choice, privacy down.

Outside this lane (swaps), a doubt only: with_return's `own` is request.own without `fills`, so a fill's UTxO holding a token with no leg is classed as a stranger's by plan_return and comes back only if it pays its own way. DEX fills usually carry ≥ 2 ₳, so it likely holds; the swap lane may want to confirm.
chain_across_pools ignores ChainRequest.boxes (each leg is capped by its `most`). The worker uses `most`, so nothing is wrong today; noted so nobody relies on `boxes` there.
